note: Nephi traces his genealogy and explains the record kept on the plates of brass.
Nephi desires to behold and understand the vision seen by his father Lehi.
The iron rod which Lehi saw is interpreted as the word of God leading to the tree of life.
Holding fast to the rod of iron protects against the fiery darts of the adversary.
Nephi expounds the words of Isaiah to his brethren.

"Free to choose liberty and eternal life... or to choose captivity and death" and "wickedness never was happiness" both teach that agency's consequences are built into the choice itself, not arbitrarily assigned afterward.
Nephi foretells that Christ will appear unto his seed after His resurrection.
King Benjamin's angelic prophecy of Christ descending among men is realized.

"My grace is sufficient for all men that humble themselves" and "it is not requisite that a man should run faster than he has strength" both teach that the Lord's expectations are matched to what His grace actually enables, not to unaided human effort alone.

Both use the same distinctive phrase for true conversion: Alma asks "have ye experienced this mighty change in your hearts?"; King Benjamin's people already had, having "no more disposition to do evil, but to do good continually."
Abinadi quotes Isaiah 53 and expounds how God himself shall redeem his people.
Alma repents at the words of Abinadi and secretly begins preaching the gospel at the Waters of Mormon.
Abinadi's prophecy on King Noah's death by fire is fulfilled.
Alma the Younger recounts his three-day experience of repentance through remembering Jesus Christ.
Alma testifies to his son Shiblon of his miraculous conversion.

Both describe people "encircled about as if by fire" from heaven - Nephi and Lehi in a Lamanite prison, and the Nephite children surrounded by angels at Christ's own visit - the same divine manifestation, decades apart.
Samuel the Lamanite prophesies a night and a day and a night without darkness as the sign of Christ's birth - fulfilled precisely as foretold, five years later.
Samuel foretells three days of darkness, storms, and great destruction marking Christ's death on the other side of the world - fulfilled exactly as prophesied at the moment of the crucifixion.
Jesus commands the Nephite record keepers to record that many saints arose from the dead, as prophesied by Samuel.
The doctrine of Christ: the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost are one.
Moroni takes up the record after the destruction of the Nephite nation at Cumorah.
Moroni's concluding farewell and final exhortation to remember God's mercy throughout all generations.

Fórmula Editorial de Mórmon ('E assim vemos'): Firmeza dos convertidos até a morte.
